semanticAssessment: Two planted regressions, each applied in the working tree and reverted before the commit. (1) WR-40: src/domain/credential-ref.ts planted to return err({kind: denied}) for keychain:../x. The OLD test file (HEAD copy, run against the same planted parser) passed 12 of 12, because its guard "if (parsed.ok || parsed.error.kind !== invalid) return" ended the loop at the third input. The strengthened target test ran to its kind assertion and failed on it for the intended reason (actual denied, expected invalid), naming keychain:../x; the other 11 tests pass, so it is not a fixture or load fault. (2) WR-41: the five /bin/ls and /bin/cat denial commands of test/integration/run-sandbox-other-profiles.test.ts planted as /usr/bin/false (a broken program that exits 1 with no permission message). The OLD test passed 31 of 31 with that plant, because it asserted only exitCode !== 0. The strengthened denied() helper failed the test "the same holds for the moved work root, for listing either root, and for the config home that names them" on its permission-message assertion ("/usr/bin/false <moved acme-data>: the failure is a permission failure"); see additionalRuns. The plan named a nonexistent program as the plant; the sandbox executor answers that with an unavailable error that the old check() helper already asserts against, so the old test fails on it too and could not show the weakness. /usr/bin/false is the plant that the old test accepts. Both planted changes were reverted and the strengthened tests pass on the real code (credential-ref 12 of 12, sandbox file 32 of 32, including the /bin/ls and /bin/cat controls).
